source_title: Christopher Lloyd Shares Moment Princess Diana Laughed During ‘Back to the Future III’ Premiere - People.com
source_excerpt:
Lloyd starred in all three ‘Back to the Future’ films with Michael J. Fox
Christopher Lloyd remembered watching Back to the Future Part III with Princess Diana
He also remembered the part of the movie that made her laugh the most
Lloyd, who also starred in Taxi and The Addams Family , just released his memoir, In My Own Time
Christopher Lloyd had a memorable brush with royalty.
The actor, who turned 88 this month, opened up on the Oct. 29 episode of Jimmy Kimmel Live! about meeting Princess Diana at the London premiere of 1990’s Back to the Future Part III .
In the film, which marked the movie franchise’s conclusion, Lloyd’s Doc Brown ends up trapped in 1885, where Buford “Mad Dog” Tannen (Biff’s great-grandfather) wants to kill him (Thomas F. Wilson played both Biff and his grandfather). Michael J. Fox ‘s Marty McFly travels back to rescue Brown, who’s also fallen in love with Clara Clayton ( Mary Steenburgen ).
Kimmel, 58, showed Lloyd the photo of him and Princess Diana meeting before the movie screening. “Did she actually go to the movie?” he asked, and Lloyd confirmed she did.
Lloyd said that he was already in Europe filming a movie, and got invited to go to London for the premiere. “Michael J. Fox, for whatever reason, wasn’t able to be there, so I got bumped up a little bit,” he said. “And I met her in line.”
Reflecting on Princess Diana, who died in 1997 at 36, he said, “She deserved to be a princess. She had that stature, a wonderful feeling about her.”
Lloyd revealed that they also sat together during the movie, and Kimmel asked if she liked it.
“I think she did,” he said, before revealing the thing that “astonished” him about her reaction to the film.
At one point in the movie, Wilson’s Buford “Mad Dog” Tannen — in a moment that called back to other films — collapses into a cart full of manure.
“For her, it was the biggest laugh of the movie,” Lloyd said. “And I thought, this is royalty. She’s human.”
Princess Diana often attended movie premieres, with and without her then-husband King Charles, in the ‘80s and ‘90s, including 1984’s Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom , 1986’s Out of Africa , 1989’s When Harry Met Sally and 1993’s The Fugitive . She also attended the 1985 London premiere of the first Back to the Future film.
This month, Lloyd released his memoir, In My Own Time . Looking back at his life and any possible regrets he might have, the Addams Family star told PEOPLE , “I don’t think about that a lot. I feel good about the way things have gone.”
Lloyd is especially still close to his co-stars from the sitcom Taxi . Marilu Henner is “den mother,” he said, coordinating get-togethers with co-stars including Danny DeVito , Judd Hirsch , Tony Danza and Carol Kane . “There is no other cast that gets together as often as we do, the Taxi cast,” he said.
Lloyd still has his eyes on another Hollywood role. “I want to get a script with another part that I feel I can fulfill,” he told PEOPLE . “That’s what I’ve always wanted, and it’s never ceased.”
He joked, “So I worry a little bit that there might be a great role for me, old fart guy, but they decide, ‘No, no, not Lloyd. He’s 88. He’s liable to drop dead on the set.’”
In My Own Time by Christopher Lloyd is available now, wherever books are sold.
